speaker: Unknown
en: If you're just starting outbound and your reply rates are low, maybe even close to zero, this video is for you.
zh: 如果你刚开始做外呼开发，回复率很低，甚至接近于零，这个视频就是为你准备的。

speaker: Unknown
en: As the founder of my company, One Schema, I personally generated and closed millions of dollars in revenue through founder-led sales.
zh: 作为我公司 One Schema 的创始人，我通过创始人主导的销售亲自创造并成交了数百万美元的收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a visiting partner at YC, I've helped hundreds of YC companies improve their outbound.
zh: 作为 YC 的访问合伙人，我帮助过数百家 YC 公司改进他们的外呼开发。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in this video, we're going to cover eight things that you can do to improve your sales outreach.
zh: 所以在这个视频里，我们会讲八件你可以做的事情，来改进你的销售外呼。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tip number one, you want to start manual before you automate.
zh: 技巧一：你要在自动化之前先从手动开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: The biggest mistake I often see founders make, they'll come to me during office hours and they'll show me their email pipeline and it will all be automated.
zh: 我经常看到创始人犯的最大错误是，他们会在办公时间来找我，给我看他们的邮件流水线，而那全都是自动化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've loaded up a tool, they blasted out a thousand emails, and they ended up getting zero replies.
zh: 他们装好了一个工具，群发了一千封邮件，结果收到了零条回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: The biggest issue with this is if you get zero replies from a campaign that you didn't give any thought to in the first place, then at the end, when you have zero replies, you've learned nothing.
zh: 这里最大的问题是，如果你从一个你一开始完全没有花心思去想的营销活动中得到零条回复，那么到最后，当你得到零条回复时，你什么也没学到。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem could be your messaging or your company targeting, your prospect selection, your deliverability, or your subject line.
zh: 问题可能出在你的信息传达、你的公司定位、你的潜在客户选择、你的送达率，或者你的标题行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my recommendation is to do at least 100 outreaches by hand before you automate anything.
zh: 所以我的建议是，在你把任何东西自动化之前，至少手动做 100 次外呼。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's honestly probably going to end up being more.
zh: 说实话，最终很可能会不止这个数。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I say by hand, I mean genuinely by hand.
zh: 而我说的手动，是指真正意义上的手动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Spend time thinking about one individual person.
zh: 花时间思考某一个具体的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is her problem specifically?
zh: 她的具体问题是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would actually capture her attention?
zh: 什么才能真正抓住她的注意力？

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit her LinkedIn page and read about her company.
zh: 去看她的 LinkedIn 页面，读一读关于她公司的介绍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Doing this homework personally is how you'll come up with your highest converting outbound ideas.
zh: 亲自做这些功课，是你想出转化率最高的外呼创意的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tip number two.
zh: 技巧二。

speaker: Unknown
en: Targeting beats perfect messaging.
zh: 定向比完美的信息传达更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I often see founders spending hours tweaking their email copy, but they barely even think about who they're emailing.
zh: 我经常看到创始人花好几个小时打磨他们的邮件文案，但他们几乎不去想自己在给谁发邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Outbound prospecting is kind of like looking for a needle in a haystack.
zh: 外呼挖掘有点像大海捞针。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need a person that has the exact pain point that you solve or a perfectly crafted message won't even land.
zh: 你需要找到一个恰好拥有你所解决的痛点的人，否则再精心打磨的信息也不会奏效。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here's an example.
zh: 这里有一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked with a company in the winter batch who was selling an infrastructure product that should have been sold to senior engineering leaders.
zh: 我和冬季批次的一家公司合作过，他们卖的是一个基础设施产品，本应该卖给资深工程负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when I opened up his LinkedIn and looked at the prospects that he was selling to, a lot of them were DevRel managers, GTM managers, there was even a customer success manager.
zh: 但当我打开他的 LinkedIn，看他正在销售的潜在客户名单时，其中很多是 DevRel 经理、GTM 经理，甚至还有一个客户成功经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was sending hundreds of these messages and was wondering why he wasn't getting any replies.
zh: 他发了数百条这样的消息，却在纳闷为什么收不到任何回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you spend a little bit more time thinking about whether or not the person you're sending the email to actually has the pain point, you'll often end up seeing a huge increase in your reply rates.
zh: 所以，如果你多花一点时间思考你发邮件的对象是否真的有这个痛点，你往往会看到回复率的大幅提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those wrong job titles were never going to buy, no matter how good your email was.
zh: 那些错误的职位头衔是永远不会买的，无论你的邮件写得多好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you find the right job titles?
zh: 那么如何找到正确的职位头衔呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: The first thing that I typically like to do is look at the customers that you already have.
zh: 我通常喜欢做的第一件事，是看看你已有的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then look at the sales process.
zh: 然后看销售流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who is the person who is pushing the last deal to close?
zh: 是谁在推动最后一单成交？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who actually signed the contract?
zh: 是谁真正签了合同？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who is the person who paid?
zh: 是谁付的钱？

speaker: Unknown
en: Look at all of their job titles and then reach out to people who have similar profiles.
zh: 看看他们所有的职位头衔，然后去联系拥有相似画像的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should also look at who has already replied to your outbound.
zh: 你还应该看看是谁已经回复过你的外呼。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're at the very earliest stages of your journey and you don't have any customers or any replies yet, ask yourself who in the organization has the most to gain from buying your software.
zh: 如果你正处于旅程的最初阶段，还没有任何客户或任何回复，问问自己组织中的谁从购买你的软件中获益最大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's an example.
zh: 这里有一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine you're selling software that monitors employee devices for security purposes.
zh: 想象一下你在卖一款出于安全目的监控员工设备的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: A chief security officer might get fired if there's a data breach, so they would really be interested in something like this.
zh: 一位首席安全官如果发生数据泄露可能会被解雇，所以他们会对这样的东西非常感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: But an engineering manager would probably rather not be monitored at all, so they're not a great person to target.
zh: 但一位工程经理可能宁愿完全不被监控，所以他们不是一个好的定向对象。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also really important to make sure that you're reaching out to the right companies.
zh: 确保你联系的是正确的公司也非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: One mistake I'll often see companies make is they'll do a search in a tool like Sales Navigator, and it will return a bunch of profiles that maybe sort of match what they were looking for, but were actually the wrong type of company.
zh: 我经常看到公司犯的一个错误是，他们在 Sales Navigator 这样的工具里做一次搜索，返回一堆也许勉强符合他们所寻找条件的资料，但实际上却是错误类型的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, if you search for tech companies in LinkedIn Sales Navigator, you're often going to get a bunch of IT implementation consultancies.
zh: 举个例子，如果你在 LinkedIn Sales Navigator 里搜索科技公司，你经常会得到一大堆 IT 实施咨询公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you want to be really thoughtful about how you're using list building tools.
zh: 所以你要非常用心地思考如何使用列表构建工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: Verify individually that each company is a good fit for your customer or your message is going to fall on deaf ears.
zh: 逐一核实每家公司是否适合你的客户，否则你的信息就是在对牛弹琴。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you do more outbound, you'll start to discover clues about a company that indicate that they need your product.
zh: 随着你做更多外呼，你会开始发现一些关于一家公司的线索，表明他们需要你的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are called intent signals.
zh: 这些被称为意向信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: A great place to look is often at job postings, as they'll tell you a lot about a company's priorities.
zh: 一个很好的查找地方通常是招聘启事，因为它们会告诉你很多关于一家公司优先级的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Company growth is another very common intent signal.
zh: 公司增长是另一个非常常见的意向信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine you're building compensation planning software.
zh: 想象一下你在开发薪酬规划软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Companies below 100 employees probably aren't introducing levels for their employees, so they won't need your software.
zh: 100 人以下的公司可能不会为员工引入职级体系，所以他们不需要你的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Companies above 500 probably already have compensation bands set.
zh: 500 人以上的公司很可能已经设定好了薪酬带宽。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when they're crossing somewhere in that 100 employee range, that's a great intent signal that they need your product.
zh: 所以当他们处于 100 人左右的规模区间时，那就是一个很好的意图信号，表明他们需要你的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every product has signals like this.
zh: 每个产品都有这样的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your job is to discover yours.
zh: 你的任务就是找到属于你自己的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: One more thing on targeting.
zh: 关于定位再说一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: For closing your very first customers, it's also far easier to start with your warm network.
zh: 要成交你的第一批客户，从你的熟人网络入手也要容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: You really want to shake the tree to make sure you hit everyone you know because the conversion rates will be much, much higher.
zh: 你真的要使劲摇一摇那棵树，确保你联系到你认识的每一个人，因为转化率会高得多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Start with your personal warm network and then ask for interest from friends, families, investors, your college roommate, a guy you met at a cafe, truly whoever you can think of.
zh: 从你的个人熟人网络开始，向朋友、家人、投资人、你的大学室友、你在咖啡馆遇到过的某个人——真的是你能想到的任何人——询问是否有兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tip number three, craft a message worth reading.
zh: 技巧三：打造一条值得阅读的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: The single most important thing you can do in your email is to give a crisp explanation of how you can help the person that you're emailing.
zh: 你在邮件里能做的最重要的一件事，就是清晰明了地说明你能如何帮助你要发邮件的那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about the top three things that keep your buyer up at night.
zh: 想一想最让你买家夜不能寐的三件事是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would get them fired?
zh: 什么事会让他们被解雇？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would get them promoted?
zh: 什么事会让他们获得晋升？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why should they believe that you can actually help them?
zh: 他们为什么要相信你真的能帮到他们？

speaker: Unknown
en: When you write an email and the buyer thinks, that's exactly the problem that I have, they really get it.
zh: 当你写了一封邮件，买家心想：这正是我遇到的问题，那他们就真的听懂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're likely to take the call even without fully understanding or trusting your solution.
zh: 即便还没完全理解或信任你的解决方案，他们也可能会接受通话。

speaker: Unknown
en: The truth is that executives don't care about your product features.
zh: 事实是，高管们并不关心你的产品功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't care that you have blazing fast uploads.
zh: 他们不在乎你有极速的上传速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't care that your database is built in Rust.
zh: 他们不在乎你的数据库是用 Rust 构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're worried about how they're going to hit their quarterly target.
zh: 他们担心的是自己要怎么达成季度目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the product explanation, I would try to make it just one sentence.
zh: 对于产品说明，我会尽量把它压缩成一句话。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want to spend paragraphs and paragraphs of details here.
zh: 你不会想在这里花大段大段的篇幅堆细节。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's typically what the first call is for.
zh: 那通常是第一次通话要做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to make sure that you establish credibility that you're the right person to help.
zh: 你要确保建立起可信度，证明你是能提供帮助的合适人选。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two common ways to do this are first to list the names of other impressive companies that you're helping, or if you don't have that yet, talk about your very relevant background for solving this problem.
zh: 两种常见的做法是：第一，列出你正在服务的其他知名公司的名字；或者如果你还没有，就谈谈你在解决这个问题方面非常相关的背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the end of your email, you want to include a very specific call to action.
zh: 在邮件结尾，你要包含一个非常具体的行动号召。

speaker: Unknown
en: It should be something like, got 20 minutes to hop on a call this week?
zh: 它应该类似于：这周有 20 分钟打个电话吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not, does this sound interesting to you?
zh: 而不是：这个听起来对你有吸引力吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to make it really easy for them to follow up with you.
zh: 你要让他们非常容易就能跟进你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Last, you can include a calendar link or a few time slots that work for you, again, to make it really, really easy for them to schedule.
zh: 最后，你可以附上一个日历链接或几个你有空的时间段，同样是为了让他们安排起来非常非常容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to make sure to keep your emails really short.
zh: 你要确保你的邮件保持非常简短。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are extremely busy and they're going to skim your emails.
zh: 人们极其忙碌，他们会快速扫读你的邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every filler word that you use dilutes the ones that matter.
zh: 你使用的每一个废话词，都会稀释那些重要的词。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a rough guide, five to eight sentences is good for email, no more than two to five for LinkedIn.
zh: 作为一个大致的参考，邮件写五到八句比较好，LinkedIn 上不要超过两到五句。

speaker: Unknown
en: Longer than that, you should probably cut something.
zh: 再长的话，你可能就该删点什么了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's an example of an email that I think is really good.
zh: 这里有一封我认为非常好的邮件示例。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's from the founder of Apten, which is a YC company in the S24 batch.
zh: 它来自 Apten 的创始人，Apten 是 YC S24 批次的一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here are some things I really like about this email.
zh: 这封邮件有几点我非常喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, notice that it's written in a really informal tone that makes him sound like a peer.
zh: 首先，注意它是用非常随意的语气写的，让他听起来像是一个同侪。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's not using any jargon.
zh: 他没有使用任何行话。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's not trying to sound super impressive.
zh: 他没有刻意表现得非常厉害。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an email that could have come from his friend.
zh: 这封邮件完全可能出自他朋友之手。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next thing I like about this is that he establishes credibility by showing that he solved the same problem at a previous reputable company.
zh: 我喜欢的另一点是，他通过展示自己曾在一家知名公司解决过同样的问题来建立可信度。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is that first line.
zh: 就是第一行那句话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I used to be a software engineer at Tesla.
zh: 我以前是 Tesla 的软件工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got crazy good at using SMS to convert the people who visited our website into car buyers.
zh: 我们在使用 SMS 把访问我们网站的人转化为购车者这件事上做得极其出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next thing I like about this email is that it has a very clear call to action.
zh: 我喜欢这封邮件的另一点是，它有一个非常清晰的行动号召。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the end, he says, would you be open to an experiment to see if we could improve your conversion rate by using AI to reactivate leads?
zh: 在结尾，他写道：您是否愿意做一个实验，看看我们能否通过用 AI 重新激活潜在客户来提升您的转化率？

speaker: Unknown
en: As the buyer, I'm thinking, okay, is this something that I would want to experiment with?
zh: 作为买家,我会想,好,这是不是我想试验一下的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it makes it really easy for me to directly follow up with him.
zh: 这也让我很容易直接跟进他。

speaker: Unknown
en: The email also feels personalized to Sumir's company by mentioning that he noticed on their website that they collect phone numbers in the signup process.
zh: 这封邮件还让人感觉是针对 Sumir 的公司个性化的,其中提到他注意到他们网站上在注册流程中收集电话号码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And notice, he barely spends any time in the email at all explaining how this product works.
zh: 注意,他几乎没有在邮件里花任何时间解释这个产品是怎么运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He focuses exclusively on how he's going to help Sumir solve his problems.
zh: 他完全专注于他将如何帮助 Sumir 解决他的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: After you write a great message, focus on your subject line.
zh: 写好一条精彩的消息之后,把注意力放在你的主题行上。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should also pay attention to the first 20 to 30 characters of the body of your email because that's what shows up in the Gmail preview.
zh: 你还应该注意邮件正文的前 20 到 30 个字符,因为那是显示在 Gmail 预览中的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Experimentation is the best way to come up with great subject lines.
zh: 试验是想出好主题行的最佳方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I find that creative and kind of weird ones can end up being the winners.
zh: 我发现有创意的、有点怪异的主题行往往会成为赢家。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, I worked with a company selling an OpenClaw-style agent product.
zh: 比如,我曾与一家销售 OpenClaw 风格智能体产品的公司合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The subject line, broken agents, performed a lot better than the more descriptive but less interesting, better agents for every workflow.
zh: 主题行「broken agents(坏掉的智能体)」的表现比描述性更强但没那么有趣的「better agents for every workflow(为每个工作流提供更好的智能体)」好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tip number four, improve your LinkedIn profile.
zh: 技巧四,优化你的 LinkedIn 主页。

speaker: Unknown
en: If email has subject lines, LinkedIn has your profile.
zh: 如果电子邮件有主题行,那 LinkedIn 就有你的主页。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's how people decide whether or not to accept your connections and to reply.
zh: 这是人们决定是否接受你的好友请求以及是否回复的依据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here are a few quick tips for making sure that your profile is great.
zh: 这里有一些快速技巧,确保你的主页很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one is you want to make sure that you have a profile picture.
zh: 第一个是要确保你有一张头像照片。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will really increase your trust level and show your prospect that you're actually a real person.
zh: 这会真正提升你的信任度,并向你的潜在客户表明你是一个真实存在的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second is you should turn that banner on the top of your LinkedIn page into an ad for your company.
zh: 第二个是,你应该把你 LinkedIn 页面顶部的横幅变成你公司的广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: Typically, it should have a really clear and concise explanation of what your company does.
zh: 通常,它应该有一个非常清晰简洁的说明,解释你的公司是做什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make sure that you avoid jargon here as well.
zh: 确保在这里也避免使用行话。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third is you should rewrite your one-line description and your about section for your company into short, concise descriptions of what your company does, similar to what you put in your banner.
zh: 第三个是,你应该把你的单行简介和「关于」部分改写成对你公司所做事情的简短、简洁的描述,类似于你放在横幅里的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And fourth, elevate anything in your profile that a buyer would care about, like relevant, impressive experience, by cutting everything else that's irrelevant.
zh: 第四,突出你主页中买家会关心的任何内容,比如相关且令人印象深刻的经历,同时删掉所有无关的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have this really long about section that talks a lot about your hobbies and other interests and things that aren't relevant, your buyers are less likely to see the ways that you can help them.
zh: 如果你有一个很长的「关于」部分,大谈你的爱好和其他兴趣以及无关的事情,你的买家就不太容易看到你能帮助他们的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another area to invest for LinkedIn is building up your number of mutual connections.
zh: LinkedIn 上另一个值得投入的领域是积累你的共同好友数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: The number of shared contacts is the single biggest predictor of whether or not somebody is going to accept your connection request in the first place.
zh: 共同联系人的数量是决定一个人是否会首先接受你的好友请求的最大单一预测因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you should focus on building relevant mutual connections with your target audience because often people within the same customer profile are connected to each other.
zh: 所以你应该专注于与你的目标受众建立相关的共同好友关系,因为同一客户画像内的人往往彼此相连。

speaker: Unknown
en: This takes time, so you should make it a daily habit to max out your connection allowance.
zh: 这需要时间,所以你应该把它变成一个日常习惯,用满你的好友申请额度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tip number five, know what your reply rates are telling you.
zh: 技巧五,知道你的回复率在告诉你什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: At first, your reply rates might be very, very low.
zh: 一开始,你的回复率可能非常非常低。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's okay.
zh: 但没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: As long as you're getting a few replies, you have a baseline to improve on.
zh: 只要你得到了一些回复,你就有了一个可以改进的基线。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even just two to three replies on 100 emails is a great place to start iterating.
zh: 即使 100 封邮件只有两三封回复,也是一个很好的迭代起点。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm working with a founder that has on the order of two to three replies on 100 emails, here's typically the order I'll start debugging their outbound.
zh: 如果我合作的创始人 100 封邮件的回复量在两三封左右,以下通常是我开始调试他们的外呼营销的顺序。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, I'll make sure that they're contacting the right person.
zh: 首先,我会确保他们在联系对的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second, I'll make sure that they're contacting the right companies.
zh: 其次,我会确保他们在联系对的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Third, I'll make sure that their subject lines are good.
zh: 第三,我会确保他们的主题行是好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, only then, will I actually start looking at their messaging.
zh: 然后只有到那时,我才会真正开始看他们的信息内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: After that, I'll look at their materials.
zh: 在那之后,我会看他们的资料素材。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, make sure their website looks good and their LinkedIn profile looks good.
zh: 比如,确保他们的网站看起来不错,他们的 LinkedIn 主页看起来不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then finally, I'll look at deliverability.
zh: 最后,我会看送达率。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go through all six of these areas and they all seem to be reasonable and you're still getting zero replies, this often might be indicative of a deeper product market fit issue.
zh: 如果你检查了所有这六个方面,它们看起来都合理,而你仍然得到零回复,这往往可能预示着一个更深层次的产品市场匹配问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tip number six, follow up and when they reply, reply fast.
zh: 技巧六,持续跟进,而当对方回复时,要快速回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: You never want to just send one email because it's very, very possible that the person simply just missed it.
zh: 你绝不应该只发一封邮件,因为很有可能对方只是没看到而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: I typically like to follow up two to four times spaced out by a couple of days.
zh: 我通常喜欢跟进两到四次,中间间隔几天。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the last email that I send a prospect, I often send what's called a breakup message.
zh: 而我发给潜在客户的最后一封邮件,我通常会发一封所谓的「分手信」。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is something usually to the effect of, since I haven't heard back, it seems like sales tax automation isn't a priority for you right now.
zh: 这类内容通常是这样的:由于我没有收到回复,看来销售税自动化对您来说现在不是优先事项。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just let me know and I can spare your inbox.
zh: 请告诉我一声,我可以让您的收件箱清净了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll often get a reply to that one.
zh: 你往往会收到对这一封的回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: Reply rates I find are much higher on these breakup emails because it makes them really low pressure for them to say no.
zh: 我发现这类分手邮件的回复率要高得多,因为它让对方说「不」的压力非常低。

speaker: Unknown
en: A real no is actually very useful to you.
zh: 一个真实的拒绝其实对你非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: In aggregate, the many no's improve who you target in the future.
zh: 总的来说，这许多次的「不」能改善你未来瞄准的对象。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you get a reply, you should be like a heat seeking missile and that nothing is going to get between you and getting onto their calendar.
zh: 一旦你收到回复，你就应该像一枚热追踪导弹，没有任何东西能阻挡你和他们约上日程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every founder will at least once experience the very painful lesson that time kills deals.
zh: 每个创始人都会至少经历一次非常惨痛的教训：时间会杀死交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: So hopefully maybe watching this video, I will save you from that lesson.
zh: 所以希望也许通过观看这个视频，我能让你免于那个教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tip number seven, block out time for outbound.
zh: 第七条建议，为外联留出时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is actually one of the biggest mistakes that I see founders make.
zh: 这实际上是我见过的创始人犯的最大错误之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're a founder, there are going to be so many things competing for your attention.
zh: 当你是创始人时，会有太多事情争夺你的注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And outbound is typically one of the least fun things to do for most founders.
zh: 而对大多数创始人来说，外联通常是最没乐趣的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you'll find excuses to do literally anything else demanding your attention.
zh: 所以你会找借口去做任何其他争夺你注意力的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you should come up with a concrete plan.
zh: 所以你应该制定一个具体的计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: Decide how many messages am I going to send per day?
zh: 决定我每天要发多少条消息？

speaker: Unknown
en: How long does it take for me to send a typical message?
zh: 我发一条典型的消息需要多长时间？

speaker: Unknown
en: When exactly am I going to send these messages?
zh: 我具体什么时间发送这些消息？

speaker: Unknown
en: It might sound like micromanaging yourself, but I actually like to put it on my calendar to hold myself accountable.
zh: 这听起来可能像是在微管理自己，但我实际上喜欢把它放在我的日历上，来督促自己对它负责。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can also have your co-founder hold you accountable if it's hard for you to do yourself.
zh: 如果你自己很难做到，也可以让你的联合创始人来督促你。

speaker: Unknown
en: The number one difference between founders who actually succeed without bound and founders who don't is actually following through on the activity that they commit to.
zh: 在外联上真正成功的创始人和不成功的创始人之间的头号区别，其实就是坚持执行他们承诺的活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tip number eight, use the messaging from your customers.
zh: 第八条建议，使用来自你客户的话术。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best feedback on your messaging always comes from your customer, not a friend, not an advisor, and not your co-founder.
zh: 对你话术最好的反馈永远来自你的客户，不是朋友，不是顾问，也不是你的联合创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here are a couple ways that you can get great messaging from your customers.
zh: 这里有一些方法可以让你从客户那里获得好的话术。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, on the sales call, one of the first questions I like to ask is, what got your attention about my message?
zh: 首先，在销售电话上，我最喜欢问的问题之一是：我的消息中是什么吸引了你的注意？

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll typically tell you the particular lines in your message that they thought were most interesting, and you should make sure to include those in future messages.
zh: 他们通常会告诉你他们认为你的消息中最有趣的特定语句，你应该确保在未来的消息中包含这些内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also gets them open-endedly talking about their problems, which is exactly what you want in a first call anyway.
zh: 这也让他们开放地谈论他们的问题，而这正是你在第一次通话中本来就想要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing I like to do for this is ask your existing customers how they think about your product.
zh: 我喜欢做的第二件事是，问你现有的客户他们是怎么看待你的产品的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ask them the single thing that got them to buy, and then use their phrasing in future messages.
zh: 问他们促成购买的那一件事情，然后在未来的消息中使用他们的措辞。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your customers are always going to write better copy than you do.
zh: 你的客户写出来的文案永远会比你写得好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know that outbound can be a slog.
zh: 我知道外联可能是一件苦差事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have personally sent thousands of outbound emails in my life.
zh: 我这辈子亲自发过数千封外联邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before you go though, one reminder, you're the founder and that's your superpower here.
zh: 但在你离开之前，一个提醒：你是创始人，这就是你在这里的超能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: The slog also pays off because your customer knowledge will compound over time.
zh: 这份苦差事也会有回报，因为你的客户知识会随着时间不断复利。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll spot a job posting and instantly know that that company has pain.
zh: 你会看到一条招聘启事，并立刻知道那家公司有痛点。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll learn why it's better to talk about pain point A instead of pain point B with smaller companies.
zh: 你会学到为什么和小公司谈痛点 A 比谈痛点 B 更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: No salesperson or agency will ever be able to learn about your customers the way that you can.
zh: 没有任何销售员或机构能够以你能做到的方式了解你的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your outbound will only get easier over time.
zh: 你的外联只会随着时间变得越来越容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks so much for watching.
zh: 非常感谢观看。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go close some deals.
zh: 去成交一些交易吧。
